pll2d5c1-d1e3514.summary: Proposes to consider what the angels became when divided by aversion and conversion.

pll2d5c1-d1e3526.summary: Explains that soon after creation some turned to the Creator, clinging to him by charity, others turned away by hatred or envy, whose mother is pride, wishing to equal God. In the converted God's wisdom shone as in a mirror, illumining them by added grace; the averted were blinded, not by infused malice but by the absence of grace never given. Conversion made some just and aversion others unjust, both by free will.
claims: Conversion is clinging by charity; aversion is envy from pride.
The averted were blinded by absence of grace.

pl-l2d5c1.summary: Asks what the angels became when divided by turning away and turning toward God. Right after creation some turned to the Creator, clinging by charity, and were illumined by wisdom through added grace; others turned away in envy, born of pride, wishing to equal God, and were blinded, not by malice infused but by the absence of grace never given. Conversion made some just, aversion made others unjust; both were acts of free will.
claims: After creation some angels turned to God and others turned away.
To turn to God is to cling to him by charity; to turn away is hatred or envy, born of pride.
The converted were illumined by grace; the averted were blinded by lack of grace, not infused malice.
Conversion made angels just; aversion made them unjust.
Both conversion and aversion were acts of free will.
